title: A Forgotten Fossil Turns Out to Be a New Dinosaur
summary:
A dinosaur fossil sat almost unnoticed in a museum for nearly 100 years. Now scientists say it is a brand-new kind of dinosaur. It lived about 120 million years ago in what is now Britain.

Scientists led by University College London studied a piece of the dinosaur's skull. It was found on the Isle of Wight, an island near England. A museum in London got it in 1924.

The dinosaur is named Invictibellatrix amberina. The name means "unconquered female warrior." It was a megaraptoran, a meat-eater with strong arms and big curved claws.

Dr. Cassius Morrison said it was about as tall as a person and three to four meters long. It probably had feathers and ate small animals. People and dinosaurs never lived at the same time.

It is the first megaraptoran ever found in Europe. That helps show how these dinosaurs spread around the world.
why_it_matters: It shows that exciting discoveries can be hiding in museums, waiting for someone to look closely.

keywords.explanation: A fossil is what is left of a plant or animal from very long ago, saved in rock.
A meat-eater is an animal that eats other animals.
A skull is the bony part of the head.
A megaraptoran was a meat-eating dinosaur with strong arms and big curved claws.
Feathers are the soft parts that cover birds, and some dinosaurs had them too.
